claims.finding: The whole print reduces to one number that the market has already assumed favourably: at the 2026-05-26 release management gave an early FY27 framework of roughly 16-17% ARR and revenue growth, down from about 25%, and the stock fell more than 31% - 'now September 3 arrives with that same 16%-17% growth framework still sitting in plain sight... management either firms that number up and gives investors a reason it was a floor, or confirms the slowdown just as the stock has recovered off the June lows', with the explicit invalidator being 'a reiteration of 16%-17% with no upward qualifier, or any further commentary on go-to-market disruption'.
claims.why_not_priced: The document itself names the asymmetry the market has ignored: 'Zscaler shares surged roughly 9.9% in the days following strong peer earnings... that move higher is exactly the problem: the stock has already shifted to price in a constructive outcome on the current quarter.' A reiteration of an existing framework is the modal corporate outcome, and it is the outcome the price is not positioned for. This is a paid options newsletter, not a wire, and none of the mainstream previews captured in the same sweep (Zacks, StockStory, tikr, Earnings Whispers) frames the print as a guide-floor binary.
claims.independence: A separate corpus item covering the same May print from a different publisher confirms the cause independently - 'Zscaler Earnings: Sales Shakeup And Weak Guidance Overshadow AI Narrative' - and another records Evercore expecting 'a meaningful shift in Zscaler's narrative going forward' on the day of the biggest decline ever: https://www.benzinga.com/ (captured as snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 23)

claims.finding: The security complex has just demonstrated that good numbers get sold: 'Palo Alto Sinks 8% Despite 34% Revenue Growth, CrowdStrike Falls 3%, Fortinet Slips' - and Zscaler rallied 9.35% over the twenty sessions into its own print on the back of that same peer reporting season.
claims.corpus_ref: snapshots/20260902T154652Z.json item 24 (headline and stored body); the optionbeast document independently records 'Palo Alto Networks fell about 8% despite 34% revenue growth... CrowdStrike fell roughly 4% in a sympathy move despite having just reported a strong quarter of its own'
claims.why_not_priced: Each peer print is wire copy; the pattern is not aggregated, and Zscaler's own tape moved the opposite way to the lesson. When a sector sells 34% growth, the bar is not the quarter, it is the multiple - and Zscaler is the highest-multiple, slowest-guided name in the group. The corpus captures a 'Cybersecurity Valuation Multiples 2026' piece in the same sweep but I did not extract a number from it.
claims.independence: Two documents in the capture record the same peer reaction set from different publishers - the headline item and the optionbeast piece - which is a genuine cross-check rather than a single source, though both reach me through the same sweep.

claims.finding: Zscaler systematically breaks its implied move and has broken it to the downside twice at this point in the calendar: options priced about 13% before 2026-05-26 and the stock fell more than 31%; they priced 10.6% before 2026-09-03 in 2024 and it fell 20.6%; across the last eight prints it has exceeded the implied move five times. The implied move for this print is again about 13%.
claims.why_not_priced: This is primarily a magnitude finding and it is signed only mildly negative because the tail is two-sided - the same statistic shows upside breaks too. Its value is that it tells me the 13% implied and the 9.79% historical median both understate this name's event distribution, so a -6 point estimate is well inside rather than at the edge of what is plausible.
claims.independence: none - same document as finding 1; collapse to one cluster with finding 1's residual.
